in-clibanarius-tricolor.title: Blue Leg Hermit Crab
in-clibanarius-tricolor.summary: A small, reef-safe hermit crab and a staple of the cleanup crew. Eats algae and leftovers and stirs the sand.
rows: Omnivore scavenger. Nuisance algae (including hair algae and cyanobacteria), detritus and leftover food
Western Atlantic Ocean and Caribbean Sea
notes: Also helps turn over and aerate the sand.

in-stenorhynchus-seticornis.title: Arrow Crab
in-stenorhynchus-seticornis.summary: A spidery crab with long thin legs. Hardy and long-lived.
rows: About 6 in; wild record 0.8 cm (0.3 in) CW (SeaLifeBase)
With caution. Known to attack other crustaceans and small slow fish; may pick at polyps if underfed
notes: Lives around small caves and crevices.

in-limulus-polyphemus.title: Horseshoe Crab
in-limulus-polyphemus.summary: Not a true crab: an ancient relative of spiders. Young ones dig through the sand nonstop looking for worms and debris.
rows: About 2' in; wild record 60 cm (23.6 in) TL (SeaLifeBase)
Yes while small; large ones can harm fish and invertebrates, especially worms and clams
Carnivore scavenger. Digs for worms and debris; supplement with pieces of squid and shrimp
Western Atlantic: Known from the Gulf of Maine to Florida, USA and along the coast of the Gulf of Mexico from Florida to the Yucatan Peninsula
notes: Females grow larger than males, up to about 12 in across.
Moves sand around almost nonstop; needs a large sand bed.

in-percnon-gibbesi.title: Sally Lightfoot Crab
in-percnon-gibbesi.summary: A crab that grazes algae off the rocks.
rows: With caution. Large ones may catch small invertebrates and fish
Omnivore. Algae, plus dried seaweed if algae runs short

in-ciliopagurus-strigatus.title: Halloween Hermit Crab
in-ciliopagurus-strigatus.summary: A hermit crab with orange-and-red banded legs that cleans up leftovers and algae.
rows: Yes, but large ones may knock over rockwork or corals
Omnivore scavenger. Leftover food, hair algae and cyanobacteria; add dried seaweed and mysis if food runs short
Indo-Pacific: from Cocos Island to Australia
notes: Sifts and aerates the sand as it forages.

in-mithraculus-sculptus.title: Emerald Crab
in-mithraculus-sculptus.summary: A small green Caribbean crab that is one of the best-known eaters of bubble algae. Hardy and reef safe, it may get pushy if underfed.
rows: Omnivore: bubble and other algae, plus leftover food; add algae wafers or meaty bits if algae runs low
Western Atlantic: Florida, the Caribbean and the Gulf of Mexico
notes: Feed it regularly if algae runs low: underfed emerald crabs can turn aggressive toward tankmates.

in-red-leg-hermit-mexican.title: Mexican Red Leg Hermit Crab
in-red-leg-hermit-mexican.sci: Clibanarius sp. (also sold as Paguristes sp.)
in-red-leg-hermit-mexican.summary: A small red-legged hermit crab from Mexico's Pacific coast that scavenges algae and leftover food. Hardy and cheap, it is a popular clean-up crew member.
rows: Omnivore: algae, detritus and leftover food
Pacific coast of Mexico, including the Gulf of California
notes: Keep a few empty shells in the tank: hermits may attack snails to take their shells.
